themes.name: AI compute: NVIDIA's supply chain
themes.what: Nebius beat on Q3 revenue ($980.8 million vs a $907.5 million forecast) but guided 2026 revenue to the low end of $3.0 to $3.4 billion and raised 2026 capex to $27 billion from $20 to $25 billion, with $40 to $45 billion planned for 2027 (CNBC; company release, Nov 12). NBIS fell about 10% before the open after closing 154.69, up 15.44%, on Nov 11 (Massive). Separately, Nvidia's board met Nov 11 on its CEO's future after a second reported relationship; no decision was announced by about 8:30am ET Nov 12 and NVDA traded about 6% to 7% lower before the open (Yahoo Finance; Reuters).
themes.for_you: The neoclouds now spend far ahead of revenue: Nebius plans up to $45 billion of capex next year against about $3 billion of 2026 sales. NBIS is 'Wait' (chart not ready) and NVDA 'Wait'; no trade or put in either before Nvidia's Nov 17 report. AMD and AVGO rose before the open on bets that buyers spread orders away from Nvidia; neither is a setup.

themes.name: AI power and the grid
themes.what: Bloom Energy closed up 12.97% at 209.47 on Nov 11 on 18.8 million shares, about 1.4 times Nov 10's volume, and Vertiv rose 6.33% to 206.51 as CoreWeave's results revived the data center trade (Massive; TradingKey). MarketBeat put Bloom's volume about 35% above average.
themes.for_you: A one day bounce after a 26.6% October drop (Motley Fool) is not a base. BE and VRT are not swing setups; wait for a base and a pivot with 1.5x volume. No puts.

themes.name: GLP-1 and obesity
themes.what: China's drug regulator approved Lilly's oral GLP-1 orforglipron for adult weight management, the first oral GLP-1 for obesity approved there; a type 2 diabetes filing is under review (Lilly China via PharmaPhorum and European Pharmaceutical Review, Nov 12). LLY rose about 2.8% before the open (Investing.com via Yahoo).
themes.for_you: Long term: helps LLY's pill reach a market where China's health agency warns overweight or obesity could top 65% of people by 2030. LLY is 'Accumulate on pullback' but its price (1,432.29 on Nov 10) sits far above its zone; no buy, no put.

themes.name: Space, Quantum and Cyber: Government Funded Frontier Tech
themes.what: The FCC accepted for filing SpaceX's application to buy 546 Grain Management 800 MHz licenses covering about 100% of the US population (about $8 billion). It is not approval: petitions to deny are due Dec 1, oppositions Dec 8 and replies Dec 15 (Benzinga, Nov 11).
themes.for_you: TMUS just entered the 'Buy zone now' list (172.16 on Nov 11, zone 145.41 to 196.73). Starlink's phone service is the long run risk to carriers; the Dec 1 to Dec 15 filings are the next checkpoint. No TMUS put passes today (thin trading).

innovations.name: Transportation
innovations.what: Rechecked on the daily rotation. Joby and Archer now point to 2027 for early US passenger operations; Archer's Nov 9 FAA certificate covers only runway takeoffs and landings, and Joby's Q3 revenue outside its Blade helicopter unit was $1.9 million (AIN, Nov 10). Tesla's robotaxi now runs 24 hours a day in eight cities, and its Texas registry count (1,303) matched Waymo's (1,305) on Nov 12. The FAA drone rule still has no date.
innovations.for_you: No action. JOBY and ACHR are not on any buy list; a one year slip with $200 million or more of cash use a quarter means more share sales are likely. ARK bought ACHR again on Nov 10 and 11; a fund buy is not a setup. TSLA and GOOGL are left out: the robotaxi race between them is close, so the news does not clearly favor either.

countries.name: European Union
countries.what: UK GDP grew 0.7% in Q3 2026, the fastest in two years, with AI related activity cited as one driver despite the oil shock (Reuters Morning Bid, Nov 12). European shares hit record highs on Nov 12 as defensive names offset the Nvidia shock (Investing.com headline via Yahoo).
countries.for_you: No action. Europe is holding up better than US tech this week; no European names are on the buy list.

countries.name: Gulf (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Iran risk)
countries.what: On Nov 12 President Trump wrote that 'we don't need a deal with Iran' and told the Vice President to focus on domestic matters, after the Wall Street Journal reported the Vice President had asked to meet a top Iranian security official. Oil rose on the post; Brent was about $93.50, up 0.8%, at 8:44am ET (Yahoo Finance).
countries.for_you: Talks look less likely, so the Hormuz premium stays. No energy setups or puts. DAL is above its zone; higher fuel is a headwind.
